name: Jitsi Meet
tagline: Video meetings on your own hostname, with no participant tier and no 40-minute cut-off.

local.note: A meeting room at http://localhost:8114 is reachable from this computer and nowhere else, so the local path is a place to learn and test Jitsi rather than a room anyone else can join.

quote.text: If guest access is enabled, unauthenticated users will need to wait until a user authenticates before they can join a room. If guest access is not enabled, every user will need to authenticate before they can join.

citations.claim: Upstream lists 80/tcp, 443/tcp and 10000/udp as the ports that must be open, with 10000/udp carrying RTP media, which is why media never passes through the reverse proxy.
JVB_ADVERTISE_IPS replaces the older DOCKER_HOST_ADDRESS and is the setting that tells the videobridge which address to advertise when it runs behind NAT, which every Docker install does.

Only JICOFO_AUTH_PASSWORD and JVB_AUTH_PASSWORD are required for a web, Prosody, Jicofo and videobridge stack; upstream states the Jigasi and Jibri passwords may be skipped when those components are not used.
The containers run as an unprivileged user with uid 1000 and fail fast when a host volume they write to is not writable by that uid.

With ENABLE_AUTH and ENABLE_GUESTS both on, the generated browser config declares an authenticated domain and a separate anonymous guest domain, which is what makes the browser ask for a login before a room can be opened.

whatYouSignUpFor: Call quality is now your server's uplink. Every participant's audio and video is relayed by the videobridge on your box, so a four-person call is four streams in and up to twelve out, and a cheap VPS with a shared network interface is where that shows up first. This is the number Zoom is really selling.

Media rides UDP straight to the machine, on port 10000, not through the reverse proxy. That means one firewall rule that no other install on this site needs, and a class of failure where the page loads perfectly and the call is silent.

End-to-end encryption is not what most people assume. Calls are encrypted in transit, but the videobridge decrypts and forwards them, so your server sees the media. Jitsi ships an end-to-end mode for multi-party calls, and it is browser-dependent and turns off several features.

No cloud recording and no dial-in numbers. Recording means running Jibri, another container with a headless browser in it, and dial-in means buying a phone number from a SIP provider. Neither is in this install.

You own the moderator account. There is no database and no user directory here: the account file under /srv/jitsi/prosody is the whole authentication system, and the day it is gone nobody can open a meeting until you register one again.
